[[Cookbook:Tortilla|Tortillas]] are a type of [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] popular in [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Mexico]] and [[:Category:Central American recipes|Central America]] commonly made from [[Cookbook:Flour#Wheat Flour|wheat flour]] or [[Cookbook:Corn Masa|masa]]. This recipe is for the wheat flour variety; see [[Cookbook:Tortilla (Corn)|Corn Tortilla]] for the masa version..

== Ingredients ==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (950 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) unbleached [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Lard|lard]] or vegetable [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]]
* 1½ cups (360 ml) warm water, or more if needed
* 4 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]] (optional, for thicker and chewier tortillas)

== Procedure ==
# In a large bowl, stir together the flour, salt and baking powder. 
# With a pastry blender, a fork, or your hands, gradually work in the lard or shortening until it is all incorporated. 
# Add enough warm water to make a soft but not sticky [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. 
# Turn out onto a lightly-floured board and [[Cookbook:Kneading|knead]] for 5 minutes.
# Divide the dough into ¼ cup (3 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] / 90 g) portions and form them into balls.
# Roll each ball into a flat round about 6 [[Cookbook:Inch|inches]] (15 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]]) in diameter and ⅛ inches (0.3 cm) thick. You can use a [[Cookbook:Tortilla Press|tortilla press]] for this.
# Heat a large heavy [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]] over medium high heat. 
# Place the tortillas one at a time into the dry (or very lightly oiled) hot [[Cookbook:Skillet|skillet]]; cook until browned in spots on one side, then turn and brown the other in spots side (about 1 minute/side)
# Remove from the skillet and keep warm in cloth towel.
